bull.b: FDA agreement that planned nonclinical studies can support a Phase 2 trial, together with guidance on dosing, design and patient selection, reduces regulatory uncertainty for TTI-109 and provides a clearer path toward an IND submission and IBD development.

The exposure analysis supports sustained STAT3 inhibition at proposed doses with minimal predicted STAT1 and STAT5 effects. If confirmed clinically, this selectivity could differentiate TTI-109 from broader JAK inhibition and support development in UC and Crohn’s disease.

Minimal current debt reduces the direct burden of interest and principal obligations, giving Tvardi more flexibility than a highly leveraged clinical-stage company. This balance-sheet feature can help preserve resources for research and development while programs advance.

bear.b: Revenue has deteriorated to zero in both 2025 and the trailing period while the company remains loss-making, leaving no demonstrated commercial income stream to fund operations. Continued dependence on clinical progress makes financial performance highly sensitive to development outcomes.

Ongoing operating and free-cash-flow losses show that the business consumes substantial cash rather than funding itself. Even though burn improved from 2023–2024, continued external funding is required to sustain operations and advance clinical programs.

The sharp decline in total assets reduces financial flexibility, while the history of negative equity signals prior balance-sheet instability. Although equity later turned positive, this record increases concern about the company’s ability to withstand delays or fund development internally.
